description: An Israeli drone struck a police post in Jabaliya refugee camp on July 14, killing 11 Palestinians including the station director. The same day, Defense Minister Katz toured northern Gaza and declared the destruction 'feels good.' Over 1,100 Palestinians have been killed since the so-called ceasefire began.

faqs.answer: An Israeli drone struck a police post near Shadia School in the Al-Falouja area west of Jabalia refugee camp, killing at least 11 Palestinians including the police station director, Col. Mohammed Marwan Salem. The area was crowded with tents sheltering displaced Palestinians.
faqs.question: What happened in Jabaliya on July 14, 2026?

faqs.answer: According to the Gaza Health Ministry, 1,108 Palestinians have been killed and 3,578 wounded in Israeli attacks since the ceasefire agreement took effect on October 10, 2025. The total death toll since October 2023 exceeds 73,000.
faqs.question: How many Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began?

faqs.answer: During a tour of northern Gaza on July 14, Katz told Channel 14 that the widespread destruction 'feels good' and was 'the result of a well-thought-out policy.' He also announced plans to establish three permanent Nahal military-civilian outposts at former settlement sites inside Gaza.
faqs.question: What did Defense Minister Katz say about Gaza's destruction?

faqs.answer: The 'Yellow Zone' is an Israeli strategy of expanding military-controlled areas across Gaza, effectively creating a de facto reoccupation. Combined with West Bank settlement expansion — including 12,000 new housing units and 34 new settlements — it represents a broader pattern of territorial annexation.
faqs.question: What is the 'Yellow Zone'?

leadParagraph: Israeli forces killed at least 11 Palestinians, including Jabaliya's police chief Col. Mohammed Marwan Salem, in a drone strike on a displacement area in northern Gaza on July 14. Defense Minister Yisrael Katz simultaneously toured the ruins and boasted that the destruction 'feels good,' announcing three new military outposts. The post-ceasefire death toll has surpassed 1,100.

methodology: Reported using official statements from the Gaza Interior Ministry and Health Ministry, eyewitness accounts reported by Anadolu Agency, and coverage from Middle East Monitor, PBS, New York Times, NPR, and Al Jazeera. Casualty figures cross-referenced across multiple sources.
